primitives.note: Flash Frost has an initial passthrough hit and a separate (manual or automatic) recast explosion, each its own damage instance with its own on-cast rules
Flash Frost or a fully-formed Glacial Storm applies a refreshable 'Iced' mark on the target for 3s; Frostbite reads that mark to decide whether to double its damage
Frostbite deals double magic damage if the target is currently Iced when the projectile lands (checked on impact, not on cast)
Glacial Storm ticks damage every 0.5s (ramping through 3 half-value ticks during a 1.5s growth phase, then continuous ticks at 300% value once fully formed), plus a final forced tick on toggle-off
Flat mana costs on Q/W/E, and Glacial Storm's ongoing per-second mana drain, can meaningfully cap how much of the kit fits in a 15s window
Rebirth (health restore + bonus armor/MR while resurrecting) is read only by the survival fight, not the damage fight

needsBespoke.why: Glacial Storm's damage ramp is more structured than a generic 'dot': it deals three half-value ticks during a 1.5s growth window, then switches to a 300%-value tick once fully formed (at a tick rate the sources don't clearly restate for damage), plus a mandatory extra tick whenever it is toggled off and a cooldown that only starts once the storm visually disappears. Frostbite's conditional doubling also depends on a timed external mark (from Q or fully-formed R) that must still be active at projectile impact rather than at cast, and Flash Frost's own damage is split into two separately-timed, separately-shieldable instances (initial cast vs. recast) with cooldown starting only after the second instance resolves. Modeling all of this correctly needs explicit sequencing/state logic beyond selecting primitives generically.

proposal: Open with Flash Frost (Q) cast directly at the dummy for its passthrough damage and to apply the Iced mark.
Immediately cast Frostbite (E) while the target is Iced for doubled magic damage.
Manually recast Flash Frost's explosion on the dummy as soon as it is available, dealing the explosion damage and refreshing the Iced mark and slow.

Toggle on Glacial Storm (R) on the dummy's position and leave it running continuously for the rest of the fight, since the stationary dummy stays inside it and each of R's ticks (once fully formed) keeps refreshing the Iced mark.
Recast Frostbite every time it comes off cooldown (4s) for the rest of the fight, timed so each cast lands while the target is Iced (which R's own ticks should guarantee once fully formed).
Recast Flash Frost again on cooldown throughout the fight purely for its own passthrough+explosion damage, since Frostbite is already being kept doubled by Glacial Storm's ticks.
Keep Glacial Storm toggled on for the full ~15s rather than turning it off early, since turning it off both forces a wait for the post-effect cooldown and only grants one extra forced tick.
questions: Is the simulated Anivia assumed to have enough mana (e.g. via items/runes) to sustain Glacial Storm's per-second drain plus Q/E costs for the full 15s, or does she realistically run out and have to toggle it off partway through?

Should Frostbite be cast strictly on cooldown regardless of the Iced state (for baseline DPS), or should its timing be adjusted to guarantee it always lands while Iced, even if that means occasionally holding it a fraction of a second?

Does Glacial Storm's growth radius (200 to 400 units) matter for a single stationary dummy assumed to be at the cast location, or should the dummy be treated as inside the zone (and therefore hit by every tick) from the moment R is cast?

Should Flash Frost's recast be timed as fast as possible after its 0.25s cast-time window, or does the automatic-max-range recast in a target-dummy setup happen at a specific delay that should instead be used for consistency with in-game play?
